```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Quantity competition has two different data layouts in trade: differentiated
products with Logit demand, and plants producing homogeneous products. This guide
uses **trade 0.9.0** with compatible antitrust/coordination dependencies and
illustrative deterministic data. Prices are currency per unit and outputs are
units. See the [tariff starter](Reference.html) ([source](https://github.com/luciu5/trade/blob/master/vignettes/Reference.Rmd)) for net-revenue margins and CV signs.

## Differentiated Logit products

Each product has its own demand and price. Firms choose their portfolio's
quantities. The Miller portfolio below contains two products.

```{r logit-cournot}
library(trade)
products <- c("BUD", "OLD STYLE", "MILLER", "MILLER-LITE",
              "OTHER-LITE", "OTHER-REG")
owner <- c("BUD", "OLD STYLE", "MILLER", "MILLER", "OTHER-LITE", "OTHER-REG")
price <- c(.0441, .0328, .0409, .0396, .0387, .0497)
quantities <- c(.066, .172, .253, .187, .099, .223) * 100
margins <- c(.3830, .5515, .5421, .5557, .4453, .3769)
tariff <- c(0, 0, 0, 0, .1, .1)
fit <- logit_cournot_tariff(prices = price, quantities = quantities,
  margins = margins, owner = owner, tariffPost = tariff, labels = products)
product_results <- data.frame(product = products,
  price_pre = antitrust::calcPrices(fit, TRUE),
  price_post = antitrust::calcPrices(fit, FALSE),
  q_pre = antitrust::calcQuantities(fit, TRUE),
  q_post = antitrust::calcQuantities(fit, FALSE))
knitr::kable(product_results, digits = 4)
```

Compare OTHER-LITE's quantity and price before/after with Miller's portfolio.
These columns are levels. The tariff `.1` is 10% of consumer price, equivalent
to a producer-value statutory rate `.1/.9`; it is not a statutory 10% rate.
With quantities converted to shares summing to one, the default standard route
uses an inside normalization product; it does not observe a positive outside
share just because quantities were supplied.

```{r logit-diagnostics}
calcDiagnostics(fit)
fitted_margin <- antitrust::calcMargins(fit, preMerger = TRUE)
margin_fit <- data.frame(product = products, observed_margin = margins,
  fitted_margin = as.numeric(fitted_margin),
  relative_discrepancy_pct = 100 * (1 - margins / as.numeric(fitted_margin)))
knitr::kable(margin_fit, digits = 4)
```

The diagnostic convention is `100 * (1 - observed/fitted)`, a relative
calibration discrepancy, not a percentage-point margin difference. BUD's
observed margin is `r sprintf("%.4f", margins[1])`, while its fitted margin is
`r sprintf("%.5f", fitted_margin[1])`; the reported discrepancy is approximately
`r sprintf("%.2f", margin_fit$relative_discrepancy_pct[1])`%, not a negative
margin of that magnitude. These illustrative observations fit this Cournot
specification **poorly on margins**, even though prices and quantities reproduce
the baseline closely. Treat this as a calibration warning before drawing
empirical conclusions. Diagnostics are not confidence intervals for the tariff
effect.

## An unobserved outside share

The ALM alternative uses additional aggregate elasticity information to estimate
the outside share. This is a different calibration assumption, not a change of
units or a mere solver setting.

```{r alm-cournot}
alm <- logit_cournot_tariff(prices = price, quantities = quantities,
  margins = margins, owner = owner, mktElast = -1.5,
  calibration = "alm", tariffPost = tariff, labels = products)
knitr::kable(data.frame(product = products,
  standard_price = antitrust::calcPrices(fit, FALSE),
  alm_price = antitrust::calcPrices(alm, FALSE)), digits = 4)
```

The supplied market elasticity is negative. Differences between the two columns
reflect different calibrated demand assumptions; they are not statistical
uncertainty bands.

## Plants producing one homogeneous product

All plants below sell the same product at a common price. A quantity matrix has
one row per plant and one column per product. We construct baseline observations
from linear inverse demand and quadratic plant costs, then impose a statutory
25% tariff on plant 1 using the consumer-price fraction `.20`.

```{r plant-cournot}
n <- 5
capacity_parameter <- c(.4, .45, .5, .55, .6)
intercept <- 10
slope <- -.25
foc <- matrix(slope, n, n)
diag(foc) <- 2 * slope - 1 / capacity_parameter
q0 <- as.numeric(solve(foc, rep(-intercept, n)))
p0 <- intercept + slope * sum(q0)
mc0 <- q0 / capacity_parameter
margin0 <- 1 - mc0 / p0
plant_tariff <- matrix(c(.25 / 1.25, rep(0, n - 1)), ncol = 1)
plant <- cournot_tariff(prices = p0, quantities = matrix(q0, ncol = 1),
  margins = matrix(margin0, ncol = 1), owner = diag(n),
  tariffPre = matrix(0, n, 1), tariffPost = plant_tariff)
plant_q_pre <- antitrust::calcQuantities(plant, TRUE)
plant_q_post <- antitrust::calcQuantities(plant, FALSE)
knitr::kable(data.frame(plant = seq_len(n), q_pre = as.numeric(plant_q_pre),
  q_post = as.numeric(plant_q_post)), digits = 3)
c(price_pre = antitrust::calcPrices(plant, TRUE),
  price_post = antitrust::calcPrices(plant, FALSE))
```

`capacity_parameter` controls the curvature of cost (`MC=q/capacity_parameter`);
it is not a hard capacity limit. Actual plant capacity constraints use the
constructor's `capacitiesPre`/`capacitiesPost` arguments. Compare the foreign
plant's response with the other four plants while remembering the product price
is common to all plants.

```{r plant-baseline-check, include=FALSE}
stopifnot(max(abs(as.numeric(plant_q_pre) - q0)) < 1e-3,
          all(is.finite(plant_q_post)), all(plant_q_post >= 0))
```

## Ownership and solver limits

| Model | Input layout | Relevant constraint |
|---|---|---|
| `logit_cournot_tariff()` | Product vectors | Valid interior solution for active differentiated products |
| `cournot_tariff()` | Plant × product matrices | Nonnegative output and plant capacity complementarity |

For commonly owned plants, marginal revenue includes the retained revenue from
all owned output affected by a quantity change. Unequal tariffs within that
portfolio require the corresponding product/plant retention weights. Ownership
itself remains the actual ownership matrix. Do not add the policy wedge a second
time as a physical cost shock or copy a universal ownership-row scaling recipe.

The homogeneous solver can handle output corners; differentiated mixed-retention
support does not imply automatic selection of zero-output products. Exit must be
specified through the supported route. Compare demand/cost specifications and
input sensitivity when applying either model; a solved toy example does not
establish the assumptions for an empirical market.

See `?logit_cournot_tariff`, `?cournot_tariff`, `trade::supportedModels()` and the
[mathematical reference](https://github.com/luciu5/trade/blob/master/doc/tariff_game_math.md).
The reference separates retained-revenue equations from effective-cost shortcuts
and preserves the longer demand and calibration background.
